problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained optimization on R^d, permitting nonconvex differentiable objectives with globally L-Lipschitz gradient and f(x0) − inf f ≤ Δ. No minimizer attainment is required. Public parameters satisfy L > 0, Λ ≥ 0, σ ≥ 0, Δ ≥ 0 and ε > 0.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SymmetricFirstMomentNonconvex.lean: Params; spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A query (x,y) returns (g(x,ω),g(y,ω)) using one shared sample; successive calls use IID samples. The jointly measurable estimator is integrable and unbiased at every point. One oracle call counts the pair of gradient evaluations. All Params are public; f, g and the sampling laws are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SymmetricFirstMomentNonconvex.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.Public and spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: gradient_similarity
distinctive_assumptions.details: The centered noise satisfies E‖η(x,ω) − η(y,ω)‖₂ ≤ Λ‖x−y‖₂ under the same sample ω. This is first-moment regularity of noise differences, not mean-square smoothness.

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: For η(x,ω) = g(x,ω) − ∇f(x), E‖η(x,ω)‖₂ ≤ σ uniformly in x. No second moment or moment of order greater than one is assumed; infinite variance is permitted.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SymmetricFirstMomentNonconvex.lean: spec.admissible, integrability and first absolute moment clauses.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is Euclidean R^d with its ℓ₂ norm, for public d ∈ ℕ.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x and coordinate i, η_i(x,ω) and −η_i(x,ω) have identical distributions. Only coordinatewise marginal symmetry is required; neither joint central symmetry nor independence between coordinates is assumed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SymmetricFirstMomentNonconvex.lean: spec.admissible, final equality of pushforward probability measures.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Return a measurable point X ∈ R^d with integrable gradient norm and E‖∇f(X)‖₂ ≤ ε. The criterion uses the norm, not its square; X need not be a specified iterate.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation includes algorithm randomness and the IID oracle sequence. The extracted budget is a fixed cap on paired oracle calls, not an expected stopping cost.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SymmetricFirstMomentNonconvex.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence; supplied extracted budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines coordinatewise symmetric noise with only a first-moment bound, first-moment regularity of centered noise differences, and shared-sample paired gradient queries. This is a meaningful specialized variant of smooth stochastic nonconvex optimization.

descriptionHtml:
Nonconvex Optimization with Symmetric Noise

We consider minimizing a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R, where d is a nonnegative integer. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz, with L>0, and a given point x0∈Rd satisfies f(x0)−infxf(x)≤Δ, with Δ≥0. Each oracle call returns unbiased stochastic gradients at two queried points using one shared sample, independently across calls. The noise has symmetric coordinate marginals, a bounded first moment, and Lipschitz dependence on the query in mean norm. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈Rd with E∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε, averaging over sampling and algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x), where ∥⋅∥ denotes the Euclidean norm. Let Ω be a measurable sample space, and let Λ,σ≥0 denote the noise regularity and first-moment bounds, respectively. The algorithm receives d, Ω with its measurable structure, L, Λ, σ, Δ, ε, and x0; the objective is accessed through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness and initial gap). The function f is differentiable everywhere, and ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈Rd,f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ,x∈Rd.

Assumption 2 (Symmetric first-moment noise). There exist a probability measure p on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:Rd×Ω→Rd. For every x∈Rd, the map g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable under p. Define the noise by e(x,ω)=g(x,ω)−∇f(x). For all x,y∈Rd, Eξ∼p[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼p∥e(x,ξ)∥≤σ,Eξ∼p∥e(x,ξ)−e(y,ξ)∥≤Λ∥x−y∥. Each coordinate marginal of the noise is symmetric about zero: for every x∈Rd and i∈{1,…,d}, ei(x,ξ)=law−ei(x,ξ),ξ∼p.

At call k≥0, the algorithm may query any pair (xk,yk)∈Rd×Rd, and the oracle returns (g(xk,ξk),g(yk,ξk)). The sample variables (ξk)k≥0 are measurable, mutually independent, and each has law p. They are independent of the algorithm’s randomness. Both replies in a pair use the same sample, and one such paired query counts as one oracle call.

After the allotted calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and ∥∇f(x¯)∥ must be integrable, with EP[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε, where P is the joint law of the samples and the independent algorithm randomness.

comparisonHtml:
f:Rd→R is differentiable with L-Lipschitz gradient and f(x0)−inff≤Δ; L,ε>0 and Λ,σ,Δ≥0. The jointly measurable, integrable oracle g is unbiased. IID samples supply paired evaluations (g(x,ξ),g(y,ξ)) with the same sample. For ζ(x,ξ)=g(x,ξ)−∇f(x), E∥ζ(x,ξ)∥≤σ, E∥ζ(x,ξ)−ζ(y,ξ)∥≤Λ∥x−y∥, and every coordinate of ζ(x,ξ) has a symmetric marginal law. Target: E∥∇f(xout)∥≤ε. Costs count primitive stochastic-gradient evaluations, including all median samples and batches; each paired query costs two evaluations.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.SymmetricFirstMomentNonconvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  Λ : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d) → ℝ
  Query q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  Reply q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  Output q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.Λ ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d) → q.Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d))
      (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
      LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
        (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
            law := P
            answer := fun _ (_, z) ω => (g z.1 ω, g z.2 ω) } ∧
      (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∀ x, f q.x0 - f x ≤ q.Δ) ∧
      Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (g x) p) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂p = gradient f x) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ∂p ≤ q.σ) ∧
      (∀ x y, ∫ ω, ‖(g x ω - gradient f x) - (g y ω - gradient f y)‖ ∂p ≤
        q.Λ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∀ x (i : Fin q.d),
        (p : Measure _).map (fun ω => (g x ω - gradient f x) i) =
        (p : Measure _).map (fun ω => -(g x ω - gradient f x) i))
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.SymmetricFirstMomentNonconvex
